## Release verified

Public [Foundryline v0.1.0](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/releases/tag/v0.1.0) is published and non-draft. GitHub returned tag `v0.1.0` pointing at the previously accepted/CI-tested commit `085ed37739b1eaed7933205a99c0ba220a1e13b6`, with published notes and tag-pinned file links. The successful [publication run](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/actions/runs/39110116925) was verified.

## This cleanup PR

- Removes the one-time `contents: write` release workflow from the repository, returning to ordinary read-only reference checks.
- Updates README, IMPLEMENTATION and the source notes to accurately link to the public release rather than saying it's still pending.
- Appends a historical publication record to the qualification review without changing the evidence scope.

The `v0.1.0` release tag remains pinned to the **original accepted commit**, intentionally excluding the temporary release automation and this post-publication housekeeping.

This PR does not create a new tag, alter the release, or publish any issues.
title: chore(release): remove temporary publisher and mark v0.1.0 published

body: The initial one-time publisher failed closed because the singular git-ref endpoint responds 404 for an absent tag; the CLI's jq output was interpreted as a conflicting value. This minimal fix uses the GitHub matching-refs endpoint, which returns `[]` when no tag exists and refuses any conflicting exact v0.1.0 tag. It preserves the accepted target commit and all other release-publication guards. Merging to `main` will retrigger the workflow and attempt the release; no issue/PR automation beyond this one-time publication.
title: fix(release): handle absent v0.1.0 tag before publication

body:
## Why
The maintainer explicitly requested **publication** of the already accepted, narrowly scoped manual Discover v0.1.0 release. The connected GitHub integration has no direct release/tag creation operation. This single-purpose GitHub Actions workflow uses the repository's own `GITHUB_TOKEN` to publish it **once** after merging to `main`.

## What the workflow does
- Runs **only** on a push to `main` changing this particular workflow file. It does **not** run on pull requests or ordinary future commits.
- Checks out the exact already-tested, accepted commit `085ed37739b1eaed7933205a99c0ba220a1e13b6`; the release tag points there, **not** to the one-off publisher.
- Converts the prepared `docs/releases/v0.1.0.md` into published release notes (removes preparation-only notices and converts local links into absolute tag-pinned URLs, rejecting broken links).
- Refuses to retarget an existing conflicting `v0.1.0` tag, and leaves an existing release untouched on rerun.
- Uses scoped `contents: write` only for the release job; source checkout credentials are not persisted.

## Safety and cleanup
This is a **one-time publication helper**, not a Foundryline scheduler or autonomous issue publisher. It should be removed from the default branch after successful verified publication to avoid lingering unnecessary privileged workflows.

**Requested effect:** Create and publish public GitHub Release `v0.1.0` with title “Foundryline v0.1.0 — Manual Discover Blueprint” at the accepted commit. No RepoTend issues or code changes are performed.

Please check GitHub Actions results and the actual releases endpoint, rather than treating a green workflow alone as confirmation.
title: chore(release): publish Foundryline v0.1.0 once from accepted commit

## Maintainer decision

The maintainer **accepted a scoped manual Discover v0.1** on 2026-10-18, as recorded in [issue #6](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/issues/6). This updates project-facing status to reflect the actual decision, without broadening the original evidence.

## Changes

- Update the welcoming README: Discover manual v0.1 accepted on the **tested macOS/Codex CLI 0.163.0 setup**; Deliver, Maintain, automatic issue creation and schedules still unqualified.
- Update IMPLEMENTATION.md with the accepted narrow qualification, unchanged host/independence uncertainty, and remaining milestones.
- Complete the decision record in `docs/discover-v0.1-qualification-review.md`, keeping the underlying R1–R8 evidence assessment intact and preserving approval identity/provenance limits.
- Add **draft** `docs/releases/v0.1.0.md` with plain-language features, real pilot evidence, caveats and getting-started links.
- Include release notes in the existing Python link/fixture checks.

## Scope of acceptance

**Accepted:** manual Discover reference, pinned public source bundle, explicitly invoked Gapline, unpublished Intentline issue proposal, fresh same-host agent reproduction, source-unavailable negative control, and supporting reference/receipt CI.

**Not accepted:** fully secure agent-host isolation, independent cross-host reproduction, automatically created issues, schedules, coding, merging, deployment, a demonstrated RepoTend runtime wrong-root write, or a published release.

## Checks

The existing GitHub Actions reference workflow will validate the updated documentation and retained receipt links. No new Codex/RepoTend runtime experiment was performed to support this editorial release-state change.

**Release publication:** This PR does **not** create a tag or a GitHub Release; those are separate authorized operations. Merge only after reviewing the scoped acceptance wording.

Refs #6.
title: docs(release): accept scoped manual Discover v0.1 and prepare release notes

body:
## Why

The current README leads with a long list of technical caveats. Foundryline's purpose—**copyable recipes for combining existing software-development tools**—should make sense to somebody seeing the project for the first time.

## What's changed

- Open with a warm, plain-English explanation of what Foundryline is and **isn't** (a cookbook/playbook, not a hosted factory or another AI agent).
- Explain the software loop and Discover / Deliver / Maintain in everyday language; clearly mark which parts are available vs. planned.
- Add a short **Try your first Discover** walk-through with copyable prompts and skill setup instructions; no Foundryline service is required.
- Use the real RepoTend pilot as a tangible example, while distinguishing a **possible source-supported issue** from a proven runtime bug.
- Keep current limitations accurate: manual pilot on one macOS/Codex host, maintainer v0.1 acceptance pending, no automatic issue writes/scheduling/merges.
- Point people to detailed design, implementation, examples, evidence and safety guidance without requiring them to understand it all before starting.

**Scope:** README-only editorial update. No workflows, code, or claims of new qualification.

## Review

Please read the opening and Try section as a first-time visitor. Could someone unfamiliar with Intentline or Gapline tell what Foundryline is, whether they can use it today, and what it will or won't do?

The existing reference-check GitHub Action will validate the README's local links. No new real-agent audit was performed as part of this rewrite.
title: docs: make README welcoming and beginner-friendly

body:
## Purpose

Prepared for [#6](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/issues/6) after reviewing [PR #5](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/pull/5) and the retained RepoTend pilot evidence.

**Recommendation:** `QUALIFY WITH STATED SCOPE` **only after explicit maintainer acceptance**. Do not treat this PR as a release approval.

## Changes

- Add `docs/discover-v0.1-qualification-review.md` with a source- and receipt-grounded assessment of issue #4's R1–R8. Classifies the read-only-host boundary, same-operator reproduction and incomplete billing/model identity as bounded or partial evidence.
- Independently spot-check the pinned RepoTend source supporting the missing-`--root` finding, retaining counterevidence and explicit `workflows.ts` scope omissions. **No target runtime defect was reproduced.**
- Clarify README and IMPLEMENTATION: the manual reference, pilot and CI checks now exist, but broad host qualification, scheduled intake and issue publication are unqualified and **the maintainer decision remains pending**.
- Extend the existing documentation integrity test inventory to check relative links in the new review document.

## Evidence and checks

- Retained pilot and reproduction event streams each show 11 `read_source` calls; negative control shows the skill read and a failed unavailable-source read.
- Last merged Foundryline main CI: [10 tests passed](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/actions/runs/39078341692).
- **This PR's** GitHub Actions checks should be reviewed before merge. No new macOS/Codex execution, RepoTend tests, security sandbox probing, or actual GitHub Copilot coding-agent invocation occurred as part of this source/receipt review.

## Maintainer decision required

Choose one:
1. **Accept scoped v0.1:** Only manual Discover on the recorded macOS/Codex setup with a pinned source-reader bundle, an unpublished issue proposal, and the published caveats. Then authorize an explicit status update.
2. **Remain pending:** Require a separately administered human/host reproduction or specific stronger host-boundary evidence before v0.1 qualification.

This PR is **not merged**, does not reclassify issue #2/#4 as fully verified, and authorizes no RepoTend issue publication or fix.

Refs #6.
title: docs: review Discover pilot evidence and propose scoped v0.1 acceptance

Validation: all 10 Foundryline structural, reader-boundary and receipt-integrity tests pass; `git diff --cached --check` passes. No RepoTend code, tests or builds were executed, and no RepoTend issue or saved Intentline agreement was created.

## Summary

Implements the **reference-artifact portion** of #2 without introducing a Foundryline runtime or an autonomous issue writer.

- Add `patterns/discover.md`: bounded read-only Gapline invocation, original-source/exception verification, duplicate checks, advisory issue drafting, optional separately authorized Intentline planning, negative paths, and qualification checklist.
- Add `examples/manual-discover/`: transparently **authored, synthetic** policy/code/test fixture; evidence-calibrated example report; **NOT PUBLISHED** issue proposal; no-findings and refusal examples; blank real-host run record.
- Add `checks/test_manual_discover.py` and a read-only `pull_request`/main integrity workflow with SHA-pinned checkout.
- Link the runbook from README and record that v0.1 remains **unqualified** pending real adoption evidence.

## Validation and limits

- Checked the contents of 14 feature-branch files and 54 local Markdown links through the GitHub connector: no missing local link targets found.
- GitHub CI runs Python stdlib reference tests **on this PR**; this is not a Gapline pilot or proof of host isolation.
- The synthetic example was *authored*, not generated by real `gapline-audit` or `intentline-issue` execution. No example target project code or tests were executed here.
- **Not yet done for #2:** actual portable skill activation in a qualified coding-agent host, one real pinned-repository pilot, independently configured reproduction, witnessed negative/refusal control, and measured actual model/tool usage. Do not close #2 or declare qualified v0.1 on merge.

## Review focus

1. Are read-only and authority boundaries accurate across Gapline, Intentline Plan and Intentline Issue?
2. Does the synthetic example correctly separate static source observations from executed evidence?
3. Is the manual procedure sufficiently copyable without a Foundryline controller?

Refs #2.

### Structural CI result

**PASSED:** [Blueprint reference checks, run #39076407506](https://github.com/grove/foundryline/actions/runs/39076407506). Python 3.12.3 ran 7 structural/documentation tests successfully. This does **not** satisfy the actual host-pilot, independent reproduction, or read-only isolation requirements in #2.
